docs.title: CA-TBL
docs.text:
Covariance-Aware Tier-Based Logic for GPS-denied search and rescue. An ns-3.47 simulation of three radio tiers, 868 MHz LoRa, 2.4 GHz LoRa time of flight and UWB, with a decision layer that escalates between them and a per-action energy model traceable to datasheet currents.

Install and build Architecture Results Source

What this is, and what it is not

This is a simulation and its measurement apparatus. Every number on this site comes from a registered campaign in the repository, run under --build-profile=optimized. No field test of the radio models has been made against hardware. The system's name is expanded in the repository's GitHub description as Covariance-Aware; older documents in the repository, and the code's identifiers (pcs*), still say confidence. They name the same system and the same score; see the uncertainty score.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text: Search and rescue in GPS-denied terrain needs both long reach and fine ranging, and no single radio delivers both. Range wants low frequency and narrow bandwidth; precision wants wide bandwidth, which shortens reach and, on a DW3000-class UWB part, makes the receive current (94 mA) larger than the transmit current (82 mA), so a precision exchange is spent mostly listening. A wearable's battery rules out keeping that radio on. The design answer is a hierarchy of radios plus a decision layer that spends precision only where it is useful and reachable. More.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
tier radio role measured reach, r80 1 868 MHz LoRa, SX1262 wide-area coverage floor; RSSI ranges, TDoA where three gateways hear a broadcast 2390 m 2 2.4 GHz LoRa, SX1280 mid-range time-of-flight refinement 320 m 3 UWB, DW3000 short-range precision, double-sided two-way ranging 5.4 m

r80 is the distance at which 80 % of frames are received, measured by the simulator's range probe under the evaluated configuration (Radios).

Every node carries all three radios. A tier is a choice of radio, not of peer. Nodes are gateways (fixed, surveyed), finders (mobile searchers with GNSS) and subjects (the field nodes being located). A five-state inertial filter carries each subject's position between fixes. The decision layer escalates one tier when a covariance-based uncertainty score falls below a per-tier threshold, subject to two suppress-only checks. Escalation.

A ≥ 0.95 at R ≤ 25 m: the share of all decision cycles with a position within 25 m. A cycle with no fix counts against it.

docs.title: Features confirmed in the repository
docs.text:
• Three physics engines (868 MHz, 2.4 GHz, UWB) with about 35 submodules each, and emergent collisions with a 6 dB capture rule.
  • A five-state IMU filter (position, heading offset, gyro bias, stride scale) with a 60-cycle window smoother and particle-filter acquisition from an unknown start.
  • Relay-aware uncertainty inflation, σ²eff = σ² + uᵀPBu.
  • A per-action energy model: charged per radio action from datasheet currents, with one tier charged per cycle.
  • Registered campaigns with a provenance sidecar (run_id.txt, SHA-256 per output) and 166 regression gates.

docs.title: Tier 1: 868 MHz
docs.text: Wide-area coverage floor, always reachable. RSSI inversion is poor as a ranging method (the error is the link's own shadowing seen from the other end), so tier 1 is a coverage floor and a coarse fix, not a ranging tier; TDoA adds a position where three gateways hear the same broadcast. Measured delivery: 0.95 at 1 km, 0.86 at 2 km, 0.71 at 3 km.

docs.title: Tier 2: 2.4 GHz
docs.text: Time-of-flight refinement, modelled on the SX1280's own 812.5 kHz row rather than the wider 1625 kHz row, a 6 dB difference. Measured delivery: 0.98 at 100 m, 0.82 at 300 m, 0.41 at 900 m.

docs.title: Tier 3: UWB
docs.text:
Short-range precision. Frames are billed, ranged and decoded in one mode. Measured delivery: 0.99 at 2 m, 0.83 at 5 m, 0.51 at 10 m, 0.14 at 20 m.

A design constant beyond a tier's reach

The evidence gate uses a 20 m prediction radius, which lies beyond the distance at which a tier-3 link delivers one frame in seven. The constant is the project's, not measured.

docs.title: Propagation
docs.text:
Each tier has its own physics engine because the differences between bands are differences of mechanism: vegetation costs a few decibels at 868 MHz and tens at UWB; the thermal floor over 499.2 MHz sits 36 dB above that over 125 kHz; and UWB detection integrates a preamble where LoRa relies on chirp processing gain. Each engine applies log-distance path loss, spatially correlated shadowing (30 m decorrelation), Rician fading with I/Q state per band, a persistent NLOS state, terrain diffraction at each tier's own carrier wavelength, and ITU-R P.833 vegetation attenuation. All tiers are simulated in the same forest, path-loss exponent drawn from \(\mathcal N(2.3,0.1)\) truncated to [2.1, 2.6], shadowing about 7 dB, foliage 0.20 dB/m saturating at 25 dB.

The path-loss exponent and shadowing values are engineering assumptions with no traced field source.

docs.title: The MAC
docs.text:
Nine message types fall into four access categories adapted from IEEE 802.11e EDCA:

class messages ACK urgent triggered update, last gasp none; 2–3× jittered rebroadcast high escalation request / grant acknowledged, the only class that is normal entry push, digest response implicit low discovery beacon none

The 9-byte MAC header (packet id, originator, hop limit, message type, tier) is common to all types, so flood control and deduplication are type-agnostic. Collisions are emergent: two overlapping transmissions collide and a 6 dB capture rule judges both frames; an interferer is attenuated by its own distance to the receiver. Before transmitting a node performs LoRa channel-activity detection and backs off for a random number of slots scaled by its access category.

docs.title: The receive chain
docs.text: A frame passes CRC, a duplicate cache keyed on the originator's packet id, a hop-limit check, the header parser and a dispatcher before it can influence a position. Because a relayed frame carries the originator in its identity field, admitting it to the poll set would insert a peer the receiver may be unable to hear; the poll set is therefore one-hop by construction.

docs.title: The per-cycle loop
docs.text:
Decisions run on a 2.5 s cycle. 2.5 s is not a tuning knob: Indian regulation caps a field node at a 2.5 % transmit duty cycle, and a tier-1 ranging frame is 56.58 ms, so the minimum compliant period is about 2.24 s (regulatory considerations).

flowchart TD
    S["Cycle k begins"] --> M["Nodes move"]
    M --> A["Range on the ACTIVE tier<br/>(chosen at cycle k-1)"]
    A --> E["Charge that tier"]
    E --> F{"≥ 3 ranges?"}
    F -- yes --> G["Use them"]
    F -- no --> H["Floor: range tier 1 in the same cycle"]
    G --> P["Estimate: EKF update, window smoother"]
    H --> P
    P --> C["Uncertainty score"]
    C --> D{"score below threshold?"}
    D -- yes --> X{"switching-point test and<br/>evidence gate pass?"}
    X -- yes --> ESC["Request escalation; on a grant,<br/>charge the handshake on the tier being left"]
    X -- no --> STAY["Stay"]
    D -- no --> DE{"N consecutive healthy cycles?"}
    DE -- yes --> DEM["De-escalate"]
    DE -- no --> STAY
    ESC & STAY & DEM --> Z["Inactive radios sleep (sleep current charged)"]
    Z --> S2["Cycle k+1"]

docs.title: The invariant the energy comparison rests on
docs.text:
Every transmission is made inside the per-cycle loop, by a radio awake that cycle, and charged to the tier that made it. A tier an arm never uses accrues its sleep current and nothing else.

This was not always true. An earlier pipeline generated all three tiers' data unconditionally and selected afterwards, under which the energy saved by not escalating was structurally unmeasurable. Fixing that is what made the energy claim testable. Any change that moves a transmission outside the loop, or charges a tier that did not transmit, breaks the only thing that gives the energy axis meaning.

The older wording, "exactly one tier transmits per cycle", has three deliberate exceptions:

  • the tier-1 floor, ranged in the same cycle when the active tier returns fewer than three ranges. The tier-1 radio stays awake and listening while another tier is active, because sleeping it clears its neighbour table; that listening is charged;
  • the dual LoRa base (--loraDualBase, in the preset): hybrid arms keep both LoRa radios awake and range both every cycle, pooling every range into one fix set, and every radio that ranged is billed;
  • the poucet_fusion comparator, which ranges every tier by design.

A UWB exchange also polls finders heard on either LoRa band that stand near the node's estimate (--uwbCrossTierPoll), because the UWB beacon is never decoded on a stint's first cycle, when the radio has just woken.

docs.title: One population of tri-band nodes
docs.text:
Every node carries all three radios; a tier is a choice of radio, not of peer. The classes differ in mobility and role only.

class mobile ids duty cap notes gateway no; surveyed, on a 15 m mast 101+ 10 % beacons on all three tiers; hosts the edge estimator finder yes 501+ 2.5 % a searcher with GNSS (2 m per axis error); registered on all tiers exactly as a gateway is subject yes 1–5 2.5 % the field node to be located; tag 0 is node 1, the lost node; may relay for other subjects

Because UWB reaches only metres, a fixed gateway offers tier 3 only to a subject already standing beside it. Tier 3 reaches a subject when a finder arrives. That is the mechanism the design rests on, and it is why the evaluation is a search rather than a monitored enclosure.

docs.title: Where the estimator runs
docs.text: The brief puts estimation on the gateways, and the preset models it there (--gatewayEdgeServer, default true since 2026-09-29). The node broadcasts, the gateways measure and report over the backhaul, and the fix returns in one downlink per fix. The filter's inputs and arithmetic are the same as node-side estimation, so only energy differs. Tiers 2 and 3 range by two-way time of flight because their endpoints share no clock; there the edge estimator only adds the downlink.

docs.title: Contributing and roadmap
docs.text: Read RULES.md before changing anything: every rule in it is load-bearing, and violating one does not produce a compile error, it produces a wrong result that looks right. CONTRIBUTING.md has the process.

docs.title: Rules that bite
docs.text:
1. Atomic commits: one change per commit, revertible in isolation, evidence in the message.
  2. Default-off flag for every new mechanism, byte-identical when off.
  3. Pre-register predictions, falsifiers and abort conditions in a PREREG_*.md committed before the first cell.
  4. A gate and its negative fixture in the same commit.
  5. Do not regenerate a tracked results directory in place, edit run_id.txt sidecars, or track trace_*.csv.
  6. Do not set hopWeight > 0 until relayed measurements exist: the poll set is one-hop, so the hop count is always 0, and a non-zero weight would degrade the score for an energy defect rather than a provenance one.
  7. Do not "fix" the score's saturation casually. It is recorded, not corrected, because a fix changes the engine and invalidates every result in the tree. It is a planned campaign, not a bug fix.
  8. Keep the fault model environmental; adversarial framing belongs only in a citation to that literature.
  9. Where a constant is ours rather than cited, the source comment must say so.

docs.title: Regression gates
docs.text:
bash scripts/catbl_gates.sh runs gates G1–G166 and reports a summary. It runs every gate and never exits on the first failure: while one gate was deliberately red, three others could not be observed to run at all.

Rules the gates follow, each earned by a real defect:

  • No gate is trusted without forced-failure evidence. Each has a negative fixture built in a temporary directory and observed to fail. A new gate ships with its fixture in the same commit.
  • Verification must not mutate its subject. A gate fails the suite if it exits with a modified tree; regeneration goes to a temporary directory.
  • Completeness gates count rows, not test for non-empty. With --seedCount=N the summary is appended per seed, so it is non-empty from the first seed.
  • Design against the failure mode. Before writing a check, write down what a firing looks like on disk; a check for a defect whose mode is absence cannot be a scan of present data.

Expected reds. G11 (the analytic link-budget model against the engine; not to be tuned, because it is the one instrument that caught the six-decibel defect) and G93 (the code default's tier-2 sensitivity row; the preset carries the data-sheet row). Any other red is a regression. RULES.md holds the current list.

docs.title: Null control
docs.text: Adding a mechanism requires a byte-identical null control: with the flag off, arm_summary.csv and every trace match the pre-change binary. Arms consume the shared random stream at their own rate, so any added transmission would perturb every arm and no before/after result would be comparable without it.

docs.title: Energy model
docs.text: Energy is a primary output: both of the project's energy claims need it. It is charged per radio action from datasheet currents, not estimated from a duty-cycle average, because the decision layer acts on the number of activations. Source: ca-tbl-energy-model.cc; specification in Architecture.md §8.

docs.title: Datasheet basis
docs.text:
SX1262 (868 MHz) SX1280 (2.4 GHz) DW3000 (UWB) TX current 45 mA @ +14 dBm 24 mA @ +12.5 dBm 82 mA RX current 5.3 mA 7.0 mA 94 mA idle 1.5 mA 1.4 mA 12 mA (PLL) sleep 1.2 µA 1.2 µA 0.7 µA supply 3.3 V 3.3 V 3.3 V

The single most consequential number

On the DW3000 the receive current exceeds the transmit current, so a UWB exchange is dominated by listening. The lever that saves UWB energy is the number of activations, which is exactly what the decision layer controls. In the 850 kb/s mode each frame also costs several times the airtime of the faster mode.

docs.text:
event charge channel-activity detection wake-up at idle plus the CAD duration at CAD current tier-1 ranging one broadcast; the node then wakes for one downlink per fix (edge estimator), on the tier the fix came from tier-2 ranging per anchor: TX, turnaround, guarded RX tier-3 ranging per anchor: TX (poll), RX (response), TX (final) failed exchange TX plus the full receive timeout, so it costs more than a success escalation handshake request TX plus guarded RX for the grant, on the tier being left inactive radios sleep current for the whole cycle neighbour discovery beacon listening at RX current edge uplink the uplink of ranges to the edge estimator, billed for every subject

The failed-exchange rule is deliberate: it makes escalating into a dead zone expensive, not merely useless.

docs.title: Time on air
docs.text:
LoRa airtime uses the Semtech relation, computed rather than assumed:

\[T_{sym}=2^{SF}/BW,\quad T_{pre}=(n_{pre}+4.25)T_{sym},\quad ToA=T_{pre}+n_{payload}T_{sym},\]

with the low-data-rate optimisation enabled automatically when \(T_{sym}>16\) ms. A tier-1 ranging frame (SF7, 125 kHz, CR 4/5, 20 B) is 56.58 ms; the escalation handshake frame is 41.22 ms. UWB airtime follows IEEE 802.15.4z HRP.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Transmit energy is recomputed from the data-sheet current, the supply voltage and the logged transmit airtime, and sleep energy from the sleep current and the run length. On 18 arm-runs (three seeds, both configurations; CA-TBL and the two static arms) transmit energy matches to a relative error of at most \(2.2\times10^{-16}\). Receive, CAD and idle energy depend on listening windows that a run does not log separately, so they are not independently recomputed.

Not modelled

Processing (CPU) energy is not in the radio model. The numbers are radio energy per subject over a 1800 s run.

docs.title: Regulatory considerations
docs.text:
No compliance claim

The simulator enforces the duty-cycle rule it models and reports the measured duty cycle. That is not a statement that any deployment complies. Compliance depends on the applicable rules, the device configuration and the operating conditions, and has not been assessed against hardware.

docs.title: The rule the model enforces
docs.text:
The governing rule is the Government of India's G.S.R. 853(E), 10 December 2021, Table II, for the 865–867 MHz band. Its text names the detection of avalanche victims as an intended use of this device category.

device class power limit duty cycle network access points (gateways) 500 mW e.r.p. 10 % other devices (field nodes, finders) 500 mW e.r.p. 2.5 %

Adaptive power control is a condition of the allowance and is implemented. Enforcement is the standard sub-GHz off-time rule: after occupying the channel for \(T\), stay silent until \(T/\text{limit}\) has elapsed. Architecture.md §7.5 records a measured tier-1 duty cycle of 0.0226 against the 0.025 cap in an earlier campaign.

docs.title: A constraint that shapes the architecture
docs.text:
quantity value tier-1 ranging frame (SF7, 125 kHz, CR 4/5, 20 B) 56.58 ms off-time armed by one frame at 2.5 % 2.263 s cycle period 2.5 s slack at cycle start +0.237 s escalation handshake frame 41.22 ms

The tier-1 budget affords about one transmission per cycle. A handoff needs two (ranging plus handshake), so a handoff costs a ranging slot at any cycle period. This is why the cycle is 2.5 s and not 1.0 s, at which a node would run at a 5.6 % duty cycle, illegal under this rule; results taken at 1.0 s are not comparable.

Regional rules differ. The 868 MHz band's rules in the EU, and the 2.4 GHz and UWB rules anywhere, are not modelled here. Anyone deploying should consult the applicable authority's current text.

cd ca-tbl-localization

The optimized profile is required

Every published number was produced under --build-profile=optimized. The default profile enables logging and runs about ten times slower on a 3600 s scenario. Gate G92 refuses a citation that an optimized build did not produce.

If the system compiler is older than GCC 11: CC=gcc-11 CXX=g++-11 ./ns3 configure .... A full build takes tens of minutes on a laptop; an incremental rebuild after editing scratch/ca_tbl_causal_sim.cc takes under a minute.

    arg=""; [ "$t" = ca_tbl_packet_validator ] && arg="--outdir=scratchpad/validator"
    printf '%s: ' "$t"; ./build/scratch/ns3.47-$t-optimized $arg 2>&1 | tail -1
done

Each suite ends with its pass and fail count; the requirement is zero failures. The full regression gates:

bash scripts/catbl_gates.sh

This takes roughly 75 to 90 minutes on a 12-core machine, runs every gate and never stops at the first red. Two reds are expected and are not build problems: G11 (the analytic link-budget model against the engine, kept red with its reasons) and G93 (the code default's tier-2 sensitivity row). See testing.

Next: quick start.

docs.text: Every new mechanism must (1) be a default-off flag whose off state reproduces the existing baseline byte for byte, (2) pass a null-control diff of arm_summary.csv and every trace, (3) be pre-registered before its first measurement run, (4) have a gate with a negative fixture, and (5) write run_id.txt with dirty 0. docs.title: From a run to a result
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    CFG["flags + preset"] --> SIM["ca_tbl_causal_sim<br/>(selected arms, one seed)"]
    SIM --> OUT["arm_summary.csv<br/>trace_*.csv, subjtrace_*.csv"]
    SIM --> RID["run_id.txt<br/>commit, dirty, profile, SHA-256 per file"]
    OUT --> GR["scripts/goal_report.py<br/>A(25 m), CEP95, energy"]

Each run writes, among other files, arm_summary.csv (one row per arm), a tag-0 trace per arm and a trace per subject. goal_report.py reads the traces' errM column and scores the design requirement; the registered analysers add paired statistics.

docs.title: Registered campaigns
docs.text:
A campaign is pre-registered: predictions, falsifiers and abort conditions are committed in report/PREREG_*.md before the first cell runs, so directory timestamps can be checked against the commit. The runner (scripts/*_run.sh) freezes one binary with a SHA-256 manifest and checks it before every cell; a cell that does not exit 0, a sidecar that is not dirty 0, more than one source, or an arm with fewer than 20 seeds aborts the campaign.

Statistics: 20 paired fresh seeds per cell; the interval is a 95 % bootstrap percentile interval of the mean paired difference, 10 000 resamples. A single-seed cross-arm difference is never a result: arms share the random stream but consume it at their own rate (two arms with identical filter state reached 334 and 336 engine evaluations by t = 2.5 s under the earlier shared stream).

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text:
Every run writes run_id.txt: the invocation, the build profile, the source commit, the count of modified tracked files, the binary's SHA-256 and a SHA-256 for each output file, written after the last stream closes. A run with dirty > 0 or a non-optimized profile is not citable.

  • 1 283 sidecars cite commit SHAs changed by an attribution rewrite on 2026-09-01; they resolve through SHA_MAP.md. Sidecars are evidence and are never edited.
  • Per-cycle trace_*.csv files are not tracked (about 13 GB); they regenerate from the recorded invocation.
  • Verification must not mutate its subject. The gate suite once regenerated tracked results in place and re-dated their sidecars; regeneration now goes to a temporary directory and a gate fails the suite if it exits with a modified tree.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text: Repeat runs from a seed are byte-identical at defaults and at six non-default flag combinations; random draws are keyed so that a transmission elsewhere no longer displaces every later draw. One tier-1 sampler ignores its seed (lora-distribution-sampler.cc); this is recorded as a decision not to fix, and no result is known to be affected.

docs.text:
When two documents disagree, the earlier one wins.

RULES.md holds the working rules and the preset list; EXCLUDED.md records what is deliberately untracked and why (for example about 13 GB of per-cycle trace_*.csv, regenerable from each directory's run_id.txt).

Working documents go stale

A "not implemented" note in a dated report may be false today. The code (the cmd.AddValue block in scratch/ca_tbl_causal_sim.cc) and the run_id.txt sidecars are the ground truth; prose is a snapshot.

docs.title: Why a hierarchy of radios
docs.text:
Satellite navigation fails in enclosed, obstructed, underground or collapsed settings, and radio reaches where satellites do not. The radio combination used here is not new: a LoRa-plus-UWB design was fielded with firefighters and soldiers (Poucet et al., IPIN 2021), and mesh LoRa localisation, threshold-based band switching, multi-hop uncertainty propagation and fault-tolerant localisation all have prior work, cited in Architecture.md §13.2.

What remains open is when combining radios pays for itself. The obstacle is physical:

  • range wants low frequency and narrow bandwidth, which leaves ranging coarse;
  • precision wants wide bandwidth, short reach, and a receive current above the transmit current, so a precision exchange spends most of its energy listening.

No single radio satisfies all three demands (reach, precision, battery). The project asks whether a decision layer that escalates between radios earns its complexity against simply pinning the radio to one tier.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Specify a three-tier stack and implement it in ns-3 with physics engines faithful enough that conclusions are about the architecture and not the simulator.
  2. Fix a design requirement in advance: A ≥ 0.95 at R ≤ 25 m, the share of all decision cycles with a position within 25 m.
  3. Compare the decision layer with pinned and fused alternatives on paired seeds, under pre-registered rules.
  4. Account for energy per radio action, so that the energy saved by not escalating is measurable.

docs.title: Contributions, stated narrowly
docs.text:
The contribution is the assembly and its quantification, plus the measurement apparatus (registered campaigns, provenance sidecars, regression gates with negative fixtures). It is not the radio combination, mesh LoRa localisation, threshold band switching, multi-hop uncertainty propagation or fault-tolerant localisation.

The fault model is environmental, not adversarial: cold-sagged battery skewing RSSI, antenna detuning from ice, canopy multipath, sensor drift.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: These are measured or recorded limits, in the repository's own words where it has them. Read them before treating a result as a statement about the real world.

docs.title: Simulation and model
docs.text:
• No hardware. Nothing here has been checked against a field node. A same-site hardware test (TECH_DEBT T45) is open.
  • Receiver sensitivity is unverified end to end. A six-decibel indexing error (sf - 7 against tables whose index 0 is SF5) sat on the tier carrying about 95 % of active cycles and passed every gate, verifier check and validation in the project. An independent closed-form model refusing to reconcile found it. No check in the project would catch a new error of that kind. Sensitivities are now read from data-sheet rows, but that is a reading, not a check.
  • Unattributed residuals. About 3.7 dB on UWB and 3.5 dB for 868 MHz near field remain unexplained; conclusions are drawn by recomputing under ±4 dB of margin offset chosen to bracket them.
  • Loss terms computed and discarded. Four loss terms (antenna gain, Doppler penalty, multipath penalty, soil attenuation) are assigned 0.0 on the line after they are computed, in the caller; in one configuration eight of sixteen terms in the loss sum were structurally zero.
  • Effective sensitivity is not a constant. A 1.5 dB link-hysteresis margin applies whenever the link was previously receiving, outside the loss sum, so the reported margin's denominator moves with the outcome and can mimic a distance-dependent effect.
  • Terrain is procedural and was not rescoped (gate G11 stays red by decision). Foliage depth is clamped to the link length.
  • Propagation assumptions. The path-loss exponent and shadowing values are engineering assumptions with no traced field source.
  • The NLOS detector is circular by construction. On a simulated channel it can only rediscover the obstructions the channel model created; its measured precision on one audit was 0.02–0.08.
  • The tier-1 ranging error is large: 1543 m mean at the distance where delivery falls to 0.8. Tier 1 is a coverage floor, and applying a time-of-arrival Cramér–Rao bound to it would be a category error (an open defect: the CRLB gate should not run on tier 1).
  • One random sampler ignores its seed (lora-distribution-sampler.cc); determinism holds and no result is known to be affected.
  • The evidence gate's 20 m radius lies beyond UWB's reach (delivery 0.14 at 20 m).

docs.title: The decision layer
docs.text:
• The escalation rule is not shown to beat a flat variance threshold; the score carries no information beyond the covariance trace.
  • The predicted-benefit rule \(\Delta J/C>\lambda\) is specified and not evaluated.
  • The integrity check does not detect most injected faults and was removed from the preset.
  • The thresholds and the dwell are fitted or the project's own choice; none was swept across environments.

docs.title: The evaluation
docs.text:
• The 5 km margin is thin: 0.952 (CI [0.911, 0.975]; 18 of 20 runs).
  • Results hold for one environment (forested, dense vegetation) and one geometry family. Different terrain, density or subject behaviour has not been evaluated.
  • The requirement is on position error within 25 m; time to first fix and convergence are not measured.
  • The deployment that meets the requirement (12 gateways, 12 finders) is not the brief's; it was found by measuring gateways × finders.
  • Energy is radio energy only; processing energy is not modelled.
  • A self-deploying gateway mesh is not implemented and is outside the brief's fixed deployment.

docs.title: Regulatory
docs.text:
The simulator models the Indian 865–867 MHz duty-cycle rule. Other jurisdictions, and the 2.4 GHz and UWB bands, are not modelled (regulatory considerations).

Open work with entry points is in docs/WORK_PACKAGES.md and docs/TECH_DEBT_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Does a decision layer that escalates between radio tiers earn its complexity against simply pinning the radio to one tier, or against fusing every radio at every cycle? The brief fixes the requirement in advance: A(25 m) ≥ 0.95.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
metric definition A(25 m) the share of all decision cycles on which a node's position estimate is within 25 m of the truth. A cycle without a fix counts by the estimate the filter holds then, which is what a searcher would be sent to; the denominator is every cycle tag 0 / five-node tag 0 is the lost node; the five-node pool is tag 0 and four peer subjects, pooled cycle by cycle CEP95 the radius containing tag 0's error on 95 % of cycles subject energy mean total radio energy of a subject over the run, joules fix share the fraction of cycles with a fix. Not the requirement; earlier campaigns reported it as "availability"

Time to first fix and time to convergence are not measured.

docs.text:

All arms share the preset's world, filter and deployment. The static arms are the control for tiering; fixed_threshold differs from the full system only in what triggers escalation, which makes it the control for the uncertainty score.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text: Each comparison is paired by seed across 20 seeds. The interval is a 95 % bootstrap percentile interval of the mean paired difference with 10 000 resamples. Predictions, falsifiers and abort conditions are committed before the first cell runs.

docs.title: What a result is
docs.text: A count, rate or sum is not an observable until its denominator, observation window and rule for observations truncated by that window are all stated. A single-seed cross-arm difference is never a result. An exact zero is a control-flow claim, not a measurement, and the code path must be proven reachable before it is reported. Every gate has a negative fixture that has been observed to fail.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text: A search, not a monitored enclosure. Twelve surveyed gateways on a 3 km ring and twelve finders in pairs; five subjects whose filters start at the box centre. 5 km is the full box (half-width 5 km); endgame is the last stretch, a 750 m half-width box with the finders converging directly, where UWB is in reach. The brief's deployment (3 gateways, 8 finders) is kept as a pinned-back variant so that every result has a before and an after.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Every number below comes from a registered campaign in the repository and is simulation only. Intervals are 95 % bootstrap percentile intervals over 20 paired seeds. The Technical Report is authoritative; report/GOAL_STATUS.md tracks the requirement campaign by campaign.

docs.title: The design requirement

docs.title: The integrity check
docs.text:
The Switching-Point Integrity Check (a Mahalanobis test of a fix against the prior; not the evidence gate) was evaluated and removed from the preset (DD 19).

The fault-free statistic's 99th percentile is 21 322 at 5 km (nominal \(\chi^2_{0.99}(2)=9.21\)), so a threshold has to be fitted to the healthy tail, and then it blinds the test. With no fault present, switching it off changes five-node A(25 m) by −0.024 [−0.056, 0.006] at 5 km, −0.002 [−0.007, 0.003] in the endgame, and +0.036 [0.003, 0.069] on INTEG3's eight-gateway ring, the one cell whose interval excludes zero. INTEG2's registered rule did not recommend keeping the test. The switching-point test, which uses other nodes' reports, stays on.

docs.title: What is not claimed
docs.text:
• That the escalation rule beats a flat variance threshold.
  • That the score carries information beyond the covariance trace.
  • That the integrity check pays.
  • Any result on hardware.

docs.title: Observables and estimation
docs.text: Each tier returns a range, or a position, and a per-measurement standard deviation. The filter consumes both. Implementation: ca-tbl-policy.cc, ca-tbl-tdoa.cc and the three lora-*-physics-engine.*.

docs.title: Tier 1: RSSI and TDoA
docs.text:
Received power is inverted through a log-distance model,

\[PL(d) = PL(d_0) + 10\,n\log_{10}(d/d_0) + X_\sigma .\]

The shadowing term is the link's own spatially correlated draw, so the range error is the shadowing seen from the other end, not independent noise. To first order \(\sigma_r = \frac{d\ln 10}{10 n}\sigma_{dB}\); the filter is given the exact standard deviation of the log-normal distribution this implies. Tier-1 uncertainty grows in proportion to range, so no fixed accuracy describes the tier, and a time-of-arrival Cramér–Rao bound does not apply to the RSSI observable.

Where three or more gateways decode the same broadcast, a TDoA position is added. Each gateway stamps the arrival on a GPS-disciplined clock; the differences are solved by Chan's closed form for four or more gateways, refined by Foy's Taylor iteration, and exactly for three. The stamp error is the clock residual plus the one-way time-of-arrival bound at the link's SNR plus an NLOS excess delay; the clock and NLOS terms are models, not measurements. A three-gateway solve has no redundancy, so a TDoA position is fused only if its normalised innovation against the state is at most 9.21, the 99th percentile of \(\chi^2\) with two degrees of freedom (--tdoaInnovationGate).

docs.title: Tier 2: two-way time of flight
docs.text: The SX1280 round-trip engine is read directly: \(\hat d = c(t_{RTT}-t_{silence})/2\), subtracting the responder's fixed turnaround. The receiver is modelled on its own 812.5 kHz data-sheet row. The precision floor is 3.0 m, from outdoor SX1280 time-of-flight measurements (Zhou et al., 2025).

docs.title: Tier 3: double-sided two-way ranging
docs.text:
A three-message exchange cancels first-order clock offset:

\[\mathrm{ToF}=\frac{T_{round,1}T_{round,2}-T_{reply,1}T_{reply,2}}{T_{round,1}+T_{round,2}+T_{reply,1}+T_{reply,2}} .\]

The radio is modelled in one data-sheet mode for everything it takes from it: 850 kb/s with a 1024-symbol preamble, at −99.3 dBm. Frames are billed, ranged and decoded in that mode. The floor is 0.10 m (Benouakta et al., 2023).

docs.title: Non-line-of-sight
docs.text: A non-line-of-sight link biases its range through the propagation layer's own state. No truth of that state reaches the filter: the variance it uses is set by a detector scoring the link from what a node can observe. The detector's measured precision on one audit was 0.02–0.08, so it flags mostly line-of-sight links, and it is circular by construction on a simulated channel.

docs.title: The filter
docs.text:
Each subject runs a five-state extended Kalman filter over planar position, heading offset, gyro bias and stride scale. Inertial increments drive the prediction, with covariance inflated by a factor of 30 because the dead-reckoner's error is coherent. Ranges are fused by sequential scalar updates; the magnetometer reading is fused as a direct measurement of the heading offset. In the preset:

element value gyro turn-on bias 0.15 °/s stride-length noise 5 % magnetometer 3° white noise plus 3° Gauss–Markov disturbance, 120 s time constant finder GNSS error 2 m per axis, carried as a consider state, not range noise window smoother last 60 cycles re-solved jointly by Levenberg–Marquardt for path, heading offset, gyro bias, stride scale and each finder's offset start every filter starts at the box centre, σ = half-width/√3; the truth reaches only the evaluation acquisition 2000-particle filter over the prior box, handing over to the EKF when the cloud is one mode

These are the project's settings for a body-worn sensor, not measurements of a specific part.

docs.title: Relayed ranges
docs.text:
A range to a node whose own position is uncertain is not a range to a surveyed anchor. With \(P_B\) that node's reported covariance and \(u\) the unit vector along the measurement,

\[\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}^2=\sigma_{\mathrm{range}}^2+u^{\mathsf T}P_B u .\]

Projecting onto \(u\) admits only the part of the neighbour's uncertainty that bears on this range. The equation applies to finders (pseudo-anchors) and to peer subjects, relaying to depth two; a relayed range is further inflated by the relay's mean normalised innovation squared, skipped if its innovation exceeds \(\chi^2_1(0.999)\), and bounded by a variance budget of \((156\,\mathrm{m})^2\) (which is the project's choice). Covariance intersection merges table entries of unknown cross-correlation.

docs.title: Two rules that must be kept apart
docs.text:
The design asks whether a more precise radio is worth activating before activating it. From the tier-1 posterior \(P_{868}\) and a predicted geometry \(H\) and noise \(R\) for the candidate radio,

\[P^+=P_{868}-P_{868}H^{\mathsf T}(HP_{868}H^{\mathsf T}+R)^{-1}HP_{868},\qquad \Delta J=\mathrm{tr}P_{868}-\mathrm{tr}P^+ ,\]

and the radio is activated when \(\Delta J/C>\lambda\) (the sensor-selection formulation of Joshi and Boyd). This rule has not been evaluated.

The implementation evaluated here is a threshold rule on the uncertainty score.

docs.title: The implemented rule
docs.text:
step behaviour escalate one tier when \(\Phi\) falls below a per-tier threshold: 1.642 from tier 1, 1.377 from tier 2 de-escalate one tier after \(N_d\) consecutive cycles with \(\Phi\) above 1.542 (tier 2) or 1.880 (tier 3) not delivered if the active tier returned fewer than three ranges, count the cycle; demote after \(N_d\). Demotion is never deferred

The gap between the two thresholds and the dwell bias the node toward staying at higher precision, on the argument that in a search a missed escalation costs more than a wasted one. The thresholds come from the calibration campaign; the dwell is the project's choice.

docs.title: Suppress-only checks
docs.text:
An escalation the score requests passes checks that can only suppress, never create, an escalation:

  1. Switching-point test. The other nodes ranged this cycle are witnesses. Witness \(j\) agrees if \(|r_j-\lVert\hat x-p_j\rVert|\le k\sqrt{\sigma_{\hat x}^2+\sigma_{p_j}^2+\sigma_\rho^2}\) with \(k=3\), \(\sigma_\rho=30\) m. With at least two witnesses, an escalation is refused if fewer than half agree.
  2. Evidence gate (2.4 GHz to UWB). Suppress unless \(\sqrt{\mathrm{tr}P}\le0.25\times20\) m and at least three UWB-capable nodes (gateways or finders) are predicted within 20 m.

Two different mechanisms

The evidence gate (above) and the integrity check (a Mahalanobis test of a fix against the prior) are different mechanisms with different measured behaviour. The repository sometimes calls both "the gate". This site does not. The integrity check is off in the preset.

docs.title: The handshake
docs.text:
An escalation is a request and a grant, sent at the highest access category. The request crosses the mesh to an arbiter, and UWB is entered only on a grant. Under the 2.5 % duty cap a tier-1 ranging frame of 56.58 ms arms 2.263 s of off-time against a 2.5 s cycle, so a handshake departing tier 1 competes with ranging for the same airtime (regulatory considerations).

Tier 3 is scarce, so the arbiter scores competing requests,

\[U(r)=\lambda_1 r_{\deg}+\lambda_2(1/E_b)+\lambda_3\zeta+\lambda_4\mathbb 1[\mathrm{query}],\]

over uncertainty-degradation rate, inverse remaining battery energy, staleness and an operator-query indicator, normalised before weighting. The \(\lambda\) encode policy, not measurement. The arbiter keeps a queue and anchors gossip their grants every 5 s.

docs.title: The uncertainty score
docs.text: Called the position-confidence score (PCS) in the code (pcsForm, pcsW1..3, pcsThr*) and in older documents. This page uses covariance-based uncertainty score because that is what the measurements show it to be.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Three terms, each in [0, 1]:

term definition \(t_1\) filter uncertainty \(\tau/(\tau+\mathrm{tr}\,P)\), \(\tau = 10\) m² \(t_2\) geometry \(1/\max(\mathrm{GDOP},1)\) \(t_3\) line-of-sight fraction from the NLOS classifier

In the evaluated form the score is a weighted sum,

\[\Phi = w_1 t_1 + w_2 t_2 + w_3 t_3,\qquad (w_1,w_2,w_3) = (2.995,\,0.000,\,0.005).\]

A fourth, hop-provenance term exists with zero weight: the poll set is one-hop by construction, so the hop count it would penalise is always zero, and a non-zero weight would change nothing except where it degraded the score for a reason unrelated to provenance. It must stay zero until relayed measurements exist.

docs.title: What the evidence says
docs.text:
The weights are the output of the project's calibration campaigns (CAL-01, CAL-03). Leave-one-seed-out calibration of the three terms ranks position error no better than the covariance trace, and the optimiser puts essentially all of the weight on \(t_1\), a monotone function of \(\mathrm{tr}\,P\). The score therefore carries no information beyond the trace, and escalating on it is escalating on the trace. In the paired comparison, CA-TBL is level with fixed_threshold, which switches on tr P > 12 m² alone (results).

The accurate name is therefore uncertainty-aware: the system acts on the filter's own covariance, and relay ranges inflate it. It is not a calibrated confidence in the statistical sense; the score is an index, and its thresholds were fitted to decisions, not to coverage.

Not claimed

That the score carries information beyond the covariance trace. The novelty claim was withdrawn (Technical Report CR-24).

docs.title: Where it travels
docs.text:
The score is carried in a one-byte field over [0, 4] (--pcsByteScale=4) so a requester can refuse a request as well as grant one. It also weights fix routing (--fixRoutingConfidence) and is returned in query responses.

Source: ca-tbl-policy.cc; preset values in kSpecProfile[].
